activity.notes: Máel Sechnaill ruled Mide from the mid-840s and achieved a wider personal supremacy conventionally represented as the high kingship of Ireland. The Dictionary of Irish Biography describes him as king of Tara, arguably the first of his dynasty to make a credible overkingship claim, and notes that the Annals of Ulster styled him 'king of all Ireland' at his death in 862. ATLAS therefore adds a separate approximate c.846-862 High Kingship Activity while preserving that this supremacy was personal and not a centralized unitary Irish kingdom.

sources.title: Máel-Sechnaill — Dictionary of Irish Biography
sources.citation_text: The Dictionary of Irish Biography identifies Máel-Sechnaill as king of Tara and a ruler who made a credible claim to the overkingship of Ireland; at his death in 862 the Annals of Ulster style him king of all Ireland.
